title: Choir Glassware
summary: Brother Decibel has finished a set of singing-glass windchimes — six strands, tuned to the lamp ring's own chord — commissioned by Keel Town for the little shrine above the moorage masts. Singing glass is to cargo what a rumour is to insurance: the payout scales with how much of the chord survives the crossing. Take the old salt pan line; it's the gentlest road on the map. The masts are a long way from the lamp ring, and every dune in between has an opinion.

objectives.label: Sign for the crated chimes at the lamp ring
Cross the flats by the old salt pan — the gentlest line
Deliver the chord to Keel Town's shrine

offer.text: Courier. Keel Town has commissioned a voice for its masts — six strands of singing glass, cut from the canyon bloom-stock and tuned to our chord. The Guild paid in full *before* hearing them, which tells you what the silence up there costs a rich person.

TUNED THEM MYSELF! — ahem. Forgive the pipes. Six strands, courier, laced in cradle-felt and crated in cork. Each one rings in the lamp ring's chord. If the crate sings on your bike, that is *normal*. If it sings a chord we did NOT tune, pull over and write it down. For science. FOR SCRIPTURE. Both.

The fee rises with the surviving chord — six strands, six notes of the payout. Singing glass does not forgive bumps, Ash. Take the salt pan; the dunes will argue, and the glass will listen to all of them.

accept.text: Ash! The chimes are nervous — glass gets stage fright, everybody knows that — so hum to them over the bumps. Any note. They just want to know the road can carry a tune. Also don't let them hear any F-naturals. Long story. Choir feud.
Copy. Cradle-felt, cork crate, hum on the bumps, avoid the feud note. Lamp ring to the salt pan to the masts. If I arrive with one strand left, does the shrine get a soloist?
A soloist is still a voice, courier. But — six would be a *choir*.

complete.text: Shrine riggers have them, courier. Struck one note against the mast weather and half of Keel Town came out onto the balconies. Nineteen years I flew this sky and never once delivered anything that made rich people go *quiet*. There's a first for every ledger.

We heard it from the hollow, Ash — faint, high, carried on the mast lines like a message that finally found its recipient. The desert's chord now has an upstairs room. Thank you for carrying it gently.
Payout's by the note and the note held. If the Guild asks, the credit was nerve management. My nerves have never been managed so musically.
